title: Wasserstein Mahalanobis Distances for Recovering Latent Geometry
summary: The Mahalanobis distance is a fundamental covariance-adapted metric for multivariate data and plays a central role in recovering latent geometry from nonlinear observations. We extend this principle from vector-valued data to probability measures by introducing a Wasserstein Mahalanobis distance. Our construction replaces Euclidean displacement vectors with optimal transport displacement fields and local covariance matrices with covariance operators defined on Wasserstein tangent spaces.
